sentences.text: Now the most dangerous half mile of your whole trip: the inlet.
Florida’s inlets are where charter boats most often get into trouble.
The worst conditions come from one combination.
A strong ebb current running out, against an onshore wind or swell coming in.
What does that do to the waves?
It stands them up and makes them break, right in the entrance.
So before you commit, stand off and watch several sets, until you understand the pattern.
Coming in, put the boat on the back of a wave, match its speed, and stay there.
Don’t run down the face, where you can broach.
And if it looks bad, wait.
Wait for slack water, wait for the flood, or use a different inlet.
Coming home a little late beats not coming home.
